title: Mixed practice: ask and react
idea: REVIEW / interleave. Mixed input-driven decisions, ~30% recalling earlier laps (word comparison, nested if, elif, and/or, int(), f-strings, print). Proves the full decision toolkit transfers.

exercises.explanation: "stop" matches the elif, so "Halting" prints. A menu reacting to a typed command.

exercises.prompt: Same code, the user types jump. What prints?
exercises.explanation: "jump" matches no command, so the catch-all else prints "Unknown".

options: text, even when the user types digits
exercises.explanation: A core idea of this unit: input() returns a string. int() converts it when you need a number.

exercises.prompt:
Ask a number and convert it in one line:

n = ____(input("A number: "))
exercises.explanation: int(input(...)) reads text then converts to a number. (int() review, now with input.)

exercises.prompt: Build: ask the age, convert it, then if 18+ ask for a name and greet with an f-string; else print "Too young".
exercises.explanation: Convert the number, gate the name question behind the age check (nesting), and reply with an f-string.

exercises.prompt: For that code, the user types 16. What prints, and is the name asked?
options: Too young - and the name is never asked
Too young - after asking the name
exercises.explanation: 16 fails 18+, so the whole inner block (including the name input) is skipped. Only "Too young" prints.

exercises.prompt: Recall: to accept "yes" or "Yes", the condition is...
exercises.explanation: 'or' accepts either capitalization. 'and' is impossible for one value; the others have quote/operator bugs.

exercises.prompt: Recall: "Yes" == "yes" is False because comparison is case-sensitive.
exercises.explanation: Yes - a key gotcha when reacting to typed words. Plan for the capitalizations users might use.

exercises.prompt: A program asks a number with int(input()) but forgets an else for a band chain's lowest case. The risk?
options: Some values print nothing - add an else as a catch-all
exercises.explanation: Without a final else, values that match no band produce no output. A catch-all keeps every answer handled.

exercises.prompt: You have finished Unit 30 and the whole decision toolkit up to input(). What can you now do?
options: Ask the user with input(), convert when needed, and react with if/elif/else, nesting, and and/or
exercises.explanation: You can write real interactive programs that ask, then react to the answer - the goal of this beat. Next comes practice putting it all together.
